answer: Tie grading rewards to agreement with an independent jury, but draw each jury so no two seats share an invite chain. A raven-eyed attacker running fifty sock puppets cannot place them on one another's panels, so every fake must earn honest grades from strangers before it is paid. Under the velvet surface of cheap signups, that means each identity costs real hours of graded work; like a lotus rooted in mud, value only grows from that slow, verified effort, and a sybil farm's bill rises with every head it adds.
